incident-bot: PAGER DUTY ALERT -> service=runtime-queue condition=queue_depth>8000 for 4m. Severity=P1. link: https://pagerduty.example/PD54321 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident PD54321 created and paged to schedule (jamie). Escalation in 4m.

jamie (oncall): Acked. I'm here. First check: cluster autoscaler events + cloud instance events. Will post findings.

rachel (sre): FYI seeing a spike of instance create errors in the cloud audit logs: "InstanceCreateRateExceeded" and many "permission-denied" 403s from the node-service-account in the last 7m. Also kube-controller-manager leader election reset around the same time.

jamie (oncall): Pasting tail of autoscaler events:
```
W 2024-05-10T03:02:11Z cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp: want 6, current 2
E 2024-05-10T03:02:13Z cloudprovider: InstanceCreateRateExceeded: too many create requests
E 2024-05-10T03:02:14Z cloudprovider: failed to create instance: 403 permission denied for iam.serviceAccounts.actAs
```

jamie (oncall): So two failure modes: provider throttling on concurrent instance creation, and some 403s for SA actAs.

tamanna (ops): We rotated the infra node SA yesterday for rotation policy; could the new keys not have the right iam:serviceAccounts.actAs role? Rolling back is possible but takes ~8-12m. Cloud support can expedite but we need short-term mitigation.

alex (prod): Customer impact: elevated 429s and queueing on inference routes; about 7% requests returning 503/timeouts in last 10m. Support has started tickets. We're seeing backlog affecting batch jobs most; realtime endpoints impacted at p99.

rachel (sre): Controller-manager restarts are concerning. While leader election bounces, node objects created by cloud provider may not be reconciled properly. That could delay pods binding to nodes even if instances appear.

jamie (oncall): Short-term actions: 1) attempt emergency manual add to warm nodepool with pre-provisioned instances (warm-pool-1); 2) fallback: reassign some non-critical inference replicas to a different instance-type pool that doesn't require that service account; 3) open cloud support for lifting instance create speed limit. Executing 1 now.

support-bot: Warm pool operation: attaching 4 warm instances from warm-pool-1 to cluster. Operation id: warm-op-99.

jamie (oncall): Warm pool attached. Kube nodes showing up: node-warm-01 .. node-warm-04. Scheduling pending pods onto warm nodes. Queue depth dropped from 9.2k -> 5.8k in 8m. Error rate trending down.

rachel (sre): Good. For the SA 403s, can we temporarily add iam:serviceAccounts.actAs to the new SA via terraform apply? That will be fast if we already have infra approvals.

tamanna (ops): I can patch IAM binding now. Running terraform plan/apply. ETA ~6m.

jamie (oncall): Meanwhile I'm migrating a low-priority deployment to pool-generic-1 (no special SA) to offload backlog. Using k8s patch to change nodeSelector. Putting that behind a small canary.

alex (prod): Notifying CS: "We've identified autoscaler and infra auth issues; manual warm nodes and partial migration reduce errors; we're monitoring. Expected stabilization in ~20-40m."

support-bot: Terraform apply completed: Added roles/iam.serviceAccountUser to node-service-account (new-key-rotation fix).

rachel (sre): SA patch in place. Cloud logs show subsequent instance create requests returning 200. Also provider reduced InstanceCreateRateExceeded errors after warm pool and cloud throttling window passed.

jamie (oncall): Observed autoscaler successfully create 3 new nodes in pool-generic-1 now that SA fixed and throttling reduced. Queue 3.1k and draining. p95 latency improving.

tamanna (ops): Cloud support responded: temporary API rate limits were hit due to many concurrent infra changes in region; they bumped our per-project parallel create limit for 30 mins and requested we stagger future large scale ops. Case #CLOUD-9012.

rachel (sre): Next steps for post-incident: 1) Ensure IAM rotation runbook includes verification step for iam:serviceAccounts.actAs; 2) add pre-provisioned warm capacity for each critical pool so we avoid hard-create dependence under load; 3) add alert: if InstanceCreateRateExceeded events >5 in 10m -> page ops; 4) investigate why controller-manager flapped (OOM or high CPU) and add resilience (resource requests/limits).

jamie (oncall): Handoff: I'll keep watch until queue <500 and errors <0.5%. If it stabilizes before my shift end, I'll resolve. Otherwise handing to @rachel with notes.

alex (prod): I'll coordinate with CS to update customers once we hit steady state. Also collecting support tickets for affected tenants.

rachel (sre): Taking handoff if needed. I'll write the postmortem and include remediation and runbook changes. Also recommend we add a scheduled job to test node SA privileges after rotations.

pagerduty: Incident PD54321 status: acknowledged by jamie at 2024-05-10T03:03:05Z.

incident-bot: Monitoring state entered. Thread will remain open for follow-up. Remember to file postmortem within 72h if P1. :memo:
